newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected to weaken further.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected to weaken further.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are poised for further weakness on Friday after the Hang Seng index fell 220.19 points on Thursday, indicating a short-term top in the market, analysts said.
"Probably the market will open a bit lower. Yesterday's movement confirms a short-term peak for the market," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities.
The Hang Seng index closed at 13,310.76 on Thursday after rising earlier in the session to a record high of 13,744.30.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London fell 6.03 points to 13,304.73.
"It will probably consolidate further. There are not many foreign factors affecting the market," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Thursday was Thanksgiving Day holiday in the United States.
Analysts saw the Hang Seng consolidating around 13,000 points over the next few sessions before moving ahead.
"There has not been much profit-taking since 12,800 and I expect the market to go down a bit further in the coming few days testing the 13,000 level," said Chan.
But analysts said the medium and longer term trend was still up.
